original_question: Let G be an infinite group, and let MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) be the cardinal symmetry numbers defined using central symmetries and the cardinal-valued measures card and card^+. Must both MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) be infinite for every finite number of colors r? Equivalently, does every finite coloring of an infinite group contain monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite size?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Problem 8.4 (Protasov): the open problem asking whether, for every infinite group G and every finite cardinal r, the two cardinal symmetry numbers ms_r(G) and ms_r^+(G) are infinite.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper very closely. It has the right section-level topic (cardinal symmetry numbers of groups), the right ambient object (an infinite group G), the right two invariants (the versions built from card and card^+), the right quantifier over finitely many colors, and it includes the paper's stated equivalent reformulation in terms of monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite size.
missing_details: The paper asks this for every finite cardinal r, i.e. for every r-coloring with r finite.
The group is endowed with the full family of central symmetries of G.

To make the question stand alone, 'symmetric subset' should be spelled out: a subset A of G is symmetric if A = g A^{-1} g for some g in G, equivalently A is invariant under the central symmetry x -> g x^{-1} g.
The numbers ms_r(G) and ms_r^+(G) are the cardinal symmetry numbers from Section 8 obtained from the measures card(A)=|A| and card^+(A)=|A|^+ on the algebra of all subsets of G.

The equivalence in the paper is specifically with existence of monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite cardinality; it does not ask here for infinite or uncountable symmetric subsets.
In the surrounding context, Theorem 8.1 settles the Abelian case affirmatively, so the open problem is the extension to arbitrary infinite groups.
refined_question: Let G be an infinite group, and endow G with its family of central symmetries x -> g x^{-1} g (g in G). Let ms_r(G) and ms_r^+(G) be the corresponding cardinal symmetry numbers defined on the algebra of all subsets of G using the measures card(A)=|A| and card^+(A)=|A|^+, respectively. Is it true that for every finite cardinal r both ms_r(G) and ms_r^+(G) are infinite?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: for every infinite group G and every finite cardinal r, does every r-coloring of G contain monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite cardinality, where 'symmetric' means A = g A^{-1} g for some g in G?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Problem 8.4 in Section 8. The nearby context first defines the cardinal-valued measures card and card^+, introduces the corresponding cardinal symmetry numbers for groups with central symmetries, and then states Theorem 8.1 for infinite Abelian groups before posing Problem 8.4 for arbitrary infinite groups. This shows that the intended target is not the later question about uncountability (Problem 8.18), but precisely the infinitude question in Problem 8.4 together with its explicit equivalent coloring reformulation.
